prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. PRODUCTION REFERENCE SHEET, landscape, not a finished book page. Bold clean clear 2D children's cartoon throughout, crisp continuous dark outlines, flat clean colors, restrained smooth cel shading, no painted or grainy texture, no gouache, no embossed relief, no 3D. Original friendly readable illustration. Ordinary neutral settings; no flags, religious/political symbols or costumes. No logos, text, letters, numbers, pseudo-writing, captions, watermarks or page borders. Natural anatomy and coherent hand/prop contact. Essential content at least 8 percent inside every edge.
WD-KIT / Kit: six-year-old human boy, golden light-medium skin, short straight black side-parted hair, teal T-shirt, mustard shorts, navy sneakers. WD-ZOE / Zoe: six-year-old human girl, deep brown skin, black hair in two puffs, yellow T-shirt, plum overalls, white sneakers. Kit and Zoe have equal standing height. Include only characters needed by this exact scene, not every reference pose. Preserve exact reference identity and clothing.
Book: The Quiet Seat; World Discovery; fiction.
Setting: A bright classroom activity room, afternoon. Blue chair at a small round table, block rug several steps away, second low table at the far side.
Design locks for the book's recurring subjects/props (NOT a visibility list; never insert later objects/states prematurely): Six plain wooden blocks; One white drawing sheet; One green pencil; Blue chair
 Create a clean separated reference board on white: show the principal recurring props/animals in front, side and three-quarter views, their relative scale beside any named human cast, and a single simple location key showing the persistent setting and daylight/palette. The human character model sheet is a supporting identity reference, not content to copy wholesale. Show only the subjects this book requires. Use initial object states: Drawing and green pencil remain on round table; no thrown blocks.. For orientation, the opening location/action is: Six wooden blocks lie scattered on the rug as Zoe shifts her blue chair farther toward the round table. Exact continuity: Drawing and green pencil remain on round table; no thrown blocks.. Do not show a completed craft or later scene merely because the finished object is listed in design locks. No future story events, no captions.

visualReview.note: Direct inspection: canonical equal-height Kit/Zoe, blue chair, exactly six plain blocks, one green pencil and blank sheet; round table, separated rug and second table layouts clear.
visualReview.limits: Direct agent visual review; no classroom or physical-device observation.
